finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Missing DB index on User.clerkId
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L80)
Evidence: User model defines "clerkId String?" with no index/unique and server code calls prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId } }) in multiple endpoints (e.g., src/app/api/admin/check-admin/route.ts). That pattern causes full table scans for every clerkId lookup.  
Impact: Full-table scans on auth lookups will overwhelm the database as users grow (tens/hundreds of thousands), causing auth-related API slowdowns or outages.  
Fix: Add an index or unique constraint on clerkId (e.g., @@index([clerkId]) or make clerkId unique) and migrate/clean duplicates; prefer a unique mapping from Clerk ID → User.

[AUTH-2] Middleware silently disables auth if env var missing
File: src/middleware.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: Middleware returns NextResponse.next() and logs a warning when process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is not set, effectively skipping all auth checks.  
Impact: A missing or misconfigured env var (common during deploys) will open protected routes (including /admin and /api/admin) to anyone, causing immediate security exposure.  
Fix: Fail-closed: require server-side Clerk secret and reject requests (401/redirect) when misconfigured, and alert/CI check env presence instead of allowing requests.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-3] No caching for server-side user mapping (clerkId→user)
File: src/app/api/admin/check-admin/route.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: After auth(), code does prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId } }) on each request with no cache or memoization.  
Impact: Every protected request triggers a DB lookup (even for frequently polled admin UI), driving sustained DB load at scale.  
Fix: Cache clerkId→user mappings (in-process LRU or Redis) or store the needed user fields in the session/token to avoid per-request DB hits.

[AUTH-4] Clerk webhook: no idempotency / fragile create path
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (L1-L240)
Evidence: handleUserCreated does findUnique by email then create (or update) without idempotency keys or catching unique-constraint races; verification is present but retries can re-run creation logic.  
Impact: Retries from the webhook delivery system can cause duplicate/create failures or transient 500s, leading to missed user syncs and downstream logic breakage.  
Fix: Use upsert by Clerk id or email, catch unique-constraint errors gracefully, or persist processed webhook event IDs to guarantee idempotent handling.

[AUTH-5] Razorpay webhook lacks idempotency around updates/external calls
File: src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts (L1-L140)
Evidence: Signature verification exists, but the handler updates order status and calls Shiprocket without marking events as processed or using transactions; repeated deliveries will re-run external side effects.  
Impact: Duplicate webhook retries may update orders multiple times and create repeated external shipments/requests, causing reconciliation issues and extra costs.  
Fix: Record processed webhook event IDs or use idempotency flag on order (e.g., processedAt/eventId) and wrap DB state changes in deterministic checks/transactions before calling external services.

[AUTH-6] Admin abandoned-carts endpoint does N+1 expensive queries
File: src/app/api/admin/abandoned-carts/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Code fetches all partialCheckouts then Promise.all maps each to run prisma.cart.findUnique and then prisma.product.findUnique per cart item (N+1 per cart).  
Impact: Admin dashboard/API becomes a heavy DB hotspot under moderate usage, leading to slow responses or DB overload even when auth is correct.  
Fix: Load data in batched/joined queries (include relations in a single DB call) or paginate and limit results to avoid large fan-out queries.

--- INFO ---

[AUTH-7] Webhook signatures are verified (good)
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts and src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts
Evidence: Svix (Clerk) and HMAC (Razorpay) signature checks are present and used to verify payload authenticity.
